title: Asset management policy and Hickory Street development approved
subtitle: Interim 2024 tax levy, Town and Gown terms of reference, infrastructure funding gap and closed session on unsheltered housing
overview: Council received the 2023 asset management report cards and approved an updated Strategic Asset Management Policy {{vote:m4}}. Staff described an ongoing infrastructure funding gap and explained that keeping every asset in excellent condition is not financially sustainable. The updated policy replaces the 2019 version and adds equity and accessibility considerations to how infrastructure decisions are made.

In an evening public meeting, Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 42 and approved a zoning change for a six-storey apartment building at Hickory Street West and Hemlock Street in the Northdale neighbourhood {{vote:m7}}. The approval raises the permitted density and allows some site-specific variances. Councillors raised questions about trees along the property line, and staff said vegetation will be reviewed through site plan control. The Region of Waterloo must still approve the official plan amendment.

Council also approved the 2024 interim tax levy {{vote:m6}} and received the Town and Gown terms of reference update as information {{vote:m5}}. Council met in closed session at the start of the meeting on an unsheltered housing update, which the minutes list as a property security matter. The minutes report no public decision from that session. Members closed with community event updates.

decisions.item: Official Plan Amendment No. 42 and zoning, Hickory and Hemlock
decisions.detail: Council adopted the official plan amendment, asked the Region of Waterloo to approve it, and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-13 for the properties at 83 and 85 Hickory Street West and 265 and 267 Hemlock Street.
Council approved the revised Corporate Policy A-030, which replaces the 2019 policy.
Council approved the 2024 interim tax levy report and the related interim tax levy by-law.
Council received the asset management report cards and update as information.

decisions.item: Town and Gown terms of reference
decisions.detail: Council received the update report on the Town and Gown terms of reference as information.

debate: On asset management, one councillor asked whether projected fair or poor water assets could still meet provincial safety rules. Staff said yes, since the City must make whatever repairs are needed and is reviewing new tools for checking pipe condition.

A councillor asked where the idea that 20 to 40 percent of assets in poor condition may be reasonable came from. Staff said it is an internal view rather than an industry standard, because assets spend years in the poor category before they are replaced. Staff added that different asset classes are treated differently, for example trees.

Climate change came up as a source of uncertainty for infrastructure. Staff said they are waiting for the City's corporate climate action plan before going further. One councillor suggested the City press the federal infrastructure ministry for different municipal funding, since the gap keeps widening.

On the Hickory and Hemlock development, a councillor asked whether trees along the rear property line would be preserved, given that the neighbouring site had already been cleared. Staff said the site plan process is still under way and that trees removed must be replaced at a two-to-one ratio, or compensated for financially.

The applicant's team explained the reduced landscaped open space. Patios and entrance walkways do not count toward it under staff's interpretation. Replacing them with sod would have made the design less accessible and less functional.
